content: Fidaxomicin is a macrolide antibiotic specifically used to treat a severe intestinal condition known as Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (C. difficile-associated diarrhea). This condition is caused by a specific type of bacteria and may rarely occur after the use of antibiotics. Symptoms of this condition include persistent diarrhea, abdominal pain or cramping, and the presence of blood or mucus in the stool. Fidaxomicin works locally in the intestines and is not absorbed into the bloodstream. It is designed to target this specific bacterial infection and is not effective against other types of infections, including viral infections such as the common cold or influenza. Before starting fidaxomicin, it is important to read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. This medication is typically taken orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor. The usual dosage is twice daily, approximately every 12 hours. If you are using the liquid form of this medication, remove the bottle from the refrigerator 15 minutes before use, shake it well, and measure the dose carefully using a special measuring device or spoon. To achieve the best results, fidaxomicin should be taken at evenly spaced intervals. It is crucial to complete the full prescribed course of treatment, even if symptoms improve after a few days, to ensure the infection is fully eradicated. Common side effects of fidaxomicin may include nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain. However, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks. Serious allergic reactions to fidaxomicin are rare but may occur. If you experience symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling, severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing, seek immediate medical attention. Before taking fidaxomicin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other macrolide antibiotics (e.g., azithromycin, clarithromycin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Additionally, fidaxomicin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, fidaxomicin should only be used when clearly necessary, as it is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your healthcare provider. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Fidaxomicin has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other infections unless directed by your doctor. While taking this medication, laboratory tests (e.g., stool sample tests) may be performed to monitor your progress. Be sure to attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store fidaxomicin tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. If using the liquid form, keep it in the original bottle in the refrigerator and discard any unused medication after 12 days. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about fidaxomicin. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
